correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the construction x*(t) by exponentiating the sign-specific linear equations. Strict decrease of h on [0,L] and antisymmetry imply 0<c*<H, positive first-half and negative second-half crossing, x*(0)=x*(L)=x*(2L)=0, and transverse velocities H-c*>0 and -(H+c*)<0. The Poincaré map is increasing and convex by scalar comparison; at infinity displacement tends to +∞ on both tails. At c=c*, the crossing residence-time derivative Q=1/(H-c*)+exp(bL)/(H+c*) gives P_uu=2bQ>0 and parameter derivative P_c=-2(1-exp(-bL))/b<0. This establishes isolated fold and, by strict monotone parameter response and convexity, exactly 0/1/2 fixed points. Reversal x(t)→-x(-t) yields initial values ±u and reciprocal multipliers. Taylor gives u~sqrt(2(1-exp(-bL))/(b² Q))sqrt(c-c*), multiplier expansions 1±2bQKsqrt(c-c*). Checked the trigonometric integration and B<A/3 derivative condition. Independent solve_ivp+root finding used three choices (A,B,b) and deltas 1e-3,1e-4; P(0,c*) residual <=6e-13, symmetric roots and predicted sqrt coefficient approached correctly. Numerical tests are corroborating, not infinite proof. Verified all seven actual Git blob identities and source tree SHA.

originality.rationale: A fresh comparison of the actual mathematical implications finds no covering independent theorem. Gasull–Zhao (2023) gives global two-cycle upper bound, convexity and perturbative fold configurations, but not the exact half-wave bias functional or its explicit fold and Floquet constants. Bravo–Fernández–Ojeda (2024) restricts the coefficients to first trigonometric polynomials and develops half-map bounds, not a formula for arbitrary C^3 monotone even half-wave profiles. The older Carmona et al. cosine-reduced equation could cover the pure harmonic specialization, not the asserted arbitrary mixed-waveform class; its inaccessible text remains a priority risk. The indexed self-match was excluded as independent evidence.

value.rationale: The scalar b|x| forced oscillator is a natural exactly analyzable piecewise-linear periodic model. Determining the exact parameter at which periodic states first appear and their sharp local separation and reciprocal stability for an infinite-dimensional family of monotone symmetric forcing profiles answers more than the known universal two-cycle bound. The weighted Laplace functional distinguishes waveform shape; a mixed first/third-harmonic example shows this is not merely the classical single-sinusoid calculation. The full waveform-dependent theorem and natural bifurcation profile have plausible further use in nonlinear-oscillator comparisons.
residual_risks: The one-frequency example alone might be known and is not the source of the PASS value judgment.
No claim of general nonsymmetric forcing or global finite-distance branch asymptotics.

final_claim: For b,L>0 and an even, 2L-periodic, half-wave antisymmetric C³ forcing h with h′<0 on (0,L), x′=b|x|+h(t)-c has exactly 0/1/2 distinct forcing-periodic solutions as c<c*, c=c*, c>c*, with c*=b/(1-e^{-bL})∫_0^L e^{-bt}h(t)dt, unique semistable fold at (u,c)=(0,c*), two reversible initial values ±u(c), reciprocal Floquet multipliers and stated exact square-root asymptotic coefficient K. Includes cos t+B cos3t class for 0<=B<A/3.
limitations: General theorem depends on waveform monotonicity, evenness, and half-wave antisymmetry.
